purpose: Candesartan is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of stroke and heart attack. It is also used to treat heart failure, helping your heart pump blood more effectively. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your kidneys, heart, and brain over time.
how_it_works: Your body makes a natural chemical called angiotensin II that tightens your blood vessels and raises blood pressure. Candesartan blocks the receptor where this chemical tries to attach, so your blood vessels stay more relaxed and open. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down to a safer level.
common_side_effects: Dizziness or lightheadedness, especially when standing up quickly. You may also notice a mild headache, back pain, or mild cold-like symptoms such as a runny nose. Unlike some similar medications, candesartan is less likely to cause a dry cough.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm your unborn baby. Avoid taking potassium supplements or salt substitutes without checking with your doctor first, since this drug can raise potassium levels in your blood. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially other blood pressure drugs, pain relievers like ibuprofen, or water pills (diuretics). Contact your doctor right away if you notice swelling of your face, lips, or throat, as this can be a rare but serious reaction.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 8 to 16 mg taken once a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose up to a maximum of 32 mg per day depending on how your body responds. For heart failure, dosing usually starts lower and is increased gradually. You can take it with or without food, and it is best to take it at the same time each day.
